title: Notes Java Multiple Static And Instance Block

runs.text: 1. When should a variable be made static?
A variable should be made static when its value is common to all objects of a class.
A static variable has one common copy associated with the class rather than maintaining a separate copy for every object.
For example, if a value needs to be shared by all objects, that variable can be declared as:

blocks.text: static int count;

runs.text: This is especially useful when maintaining a common value such as the total number of objects created for a class.
2. When should a method be made static?
A method can be made static when it needs to be called without creating an object.
A static method can be called using the class name.
It is also appropriate when the method represents a generic operation that does not depend on a particular object's state.
The main idea is that object creation is not required to call a static method.

No.

The main difference is when they execute.
Static block:
Associated with the class.

created
for a class be counted?
The number of objects can be counted by maintaining a count that is updated whenever an object is created.
For example:
Three objects are created.
The required output can be:
Number of objects created for Demo class is 3
The important idea is to identify an event that occurs whenever an object is created and use that event to update the count.
12. Why can the constructor be used for counting objects?
A constructor is called at the time of object creation.
For example:

blocks.text: Demo d1 = new Demo();

runs.text: When this object is created, the constructor executes.
Therefore, every time a constructor executes for an object creation, the object count can be incremented.
The relationship can be remembered as:
Object creation → Constructor execution → Count increment
If the constructor executes five times because five objects are created, the count can become five.
13. Can a constructor be called before object creation?
The constructor is associated with object creation.
When an object is created, the constructor is called as part of that process.
For example:

blocks.text: Demo d1 = new Demo();

runs.text: The object is created and the constructor executes.
Therefore, the constructor execution is directly associated with creating the object.
14. If a constructor is executed five times, how many objects are created?
If the constructor is executed five times as part of object creation, five objects have been created.
For example:
Constructor execution → Object creation
5 constructor executions → 5 objects
This relationship can be used to design an object-counting program.

If the count variable is not static, it becomes an instance variable.

19. Why is the count accessed using the class when it is static?
When count is declared as static, it belongs to the class rather than to an individual object.
Therefore, the common count can be accessed using the class name:

22. How are objects and references represented conceptually using stack and heap?
When multiple objects are created, the objects exist in the heap, while their references can point to those objects.

Normally, a class allows multiple objects to be created.

However, some requirements may need only one object of a particular class.

24. What is a design pattern?
A design pattern is a set of rules to solve a particular problem.
It provides a defined approach for solving a problem rather than creating an unrelated solution each time.
Design Pattern = A set of rules to solve a particular problem.
The design pattern itself represents the rules. Those rules are then followed while implementing the solution.

The Singleton Design Pattern is used when a class should allow only one object to be created.

If the requirement is that the class should have only one object, the Singleton Design Pattern is used.
